Describes (1) the functional relationship between this dataset and the coupled technique — what data or context flows between them — and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique was performed first and why. Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not 'None'.

DOI of the dataset or publication containing the coupled technique data. If coupling is documented only through a shared sample IGSN (Group 2), this field may be 'None'.

Type of geological or experimental material being analyzed (e.g., basalt, chondrite, seawater, mineral separate). Constrains the dissolution strategy, chromatographic separation, and matrix-matching requirements.
Example / Allowed Content: Basalt | Chondrite | Seawater | Mineral separate | Synthetic solution | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: International Geo Sample Number (IGSN) or other persistent identifier for the sample.
Brief description of sample provenance, form, or preparation state relevant to this analysis.

General approach to mechanical sample preparation prior to dissolution (e.g., whole-rock crushing and powdering, mineral separation). Documents how the solid material was conditioned before acid digestion.
Example / Allowed Content: Whole-rock powder | Mineral separate | Dissolved residue | Pre-digested liquid | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Acid mixture used for sample dissolution. Record acid type(s) and concentration(s) where known (e.g., concentrated HF–HNO3 in Parr bombs is standard for silicate dissolution). For isotope ratio work, complete matrix dissolution is required to avoid isotopic fractionation during partial dissolution.
Example / Allowed Content: HF–HNO3 | HF–HNO3–HClO4 | HNO3–HCl | HNO3 only | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Type of vessel used for acid digestion. Vessel type constrains maximum temperature and pressure and determines suitability for refractory mineral dissolution (e.g., Parr bombs required for complete silicate digestion at high temperatures).
Example / Allowed Content: Savillex beaker | Parr bomb | TFE/TFM bomb | Carius tube | HPA-S | Open beaker | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Total number of distinct acid digestion steps required to dissolve the sample. Some procedures require multiple sequential steps (e.g., open-beaker HF–HNO3 dissolution followed by aqua regia reflux to destroy fluoride complexes).
Temperature at which acid digestion was carried out (°C). Procedure specifies the target temperature.
Duration of the primary acid digestion step (hours or days).

Acid type and concentration of the final dissolved sample solution introduced to the instrument. Critical for isotope ratio work: acid molarity must be precisely matched between samples and bracketing standards to avoid matrix-induced mass bias offsets.
Example / Allowed Content: 0.3 M HNO3 | 2% HNO3 | 0.5 M HCl | 3 M HCl | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Mass (mg) of solid material digested or volume (mL) of liquid taken for dissolution. Used for yield calculations and concentration back-calculation in isotope dilution procedures.

Whether chromatographic separation was performed prior to MC-ICP-MS analysis. Separation is usually mandatory for solution MC-ICP-MS to remove matrix elements that cause variable mass bias and to eliminate isobaric interferences (e.g., removal of Cr and Ni from Fe fractions; separation of U from matrix). Record resin type and elution matrix. Record 'None' if direct digestion solution is analyzed (uncommon for isotope ratio work).
Example / Allowed Content: Anion exchange resin AG1-X8 (HCl) | Cation exchange resin AG50W-X8 | TRU resin | UTEVA resin | AG-MP-1 (HBr) | Thiol resin | Multi-step: specify | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Isotopic spike material added to the sample before or during digestion for isotope dilution (ID) analysis or double-spike mass bias correction. For double-spike procedures, the spike must be added and equilibrated before digestion to correct for any isotopic fractionation during dissolution and column chemistry. For concentration ID, the spike must be added before digestion for complete equilibration. Record spike name or certificate reference, spike isotopes, and whether added pre- or post-digestion. Record 'None' if ID or double-spike technique is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: IRMM-3636 (233U–236U double spike) | 117Sn–122Sn double spike (in-house) | 57Fe–58Fe double spike | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Manufacturer and model name of the MC-ICP-MS instrument. Determines the collector array geometry, available mass resolution modes, and detector complement.
Example / Allowed Content: Thermo Scientific Neptune | Thermo Scientific Neptune Plus | Nu Instruments Nu Plasma II | Nu Instruments Nu Plasma 1700 | Nu Instruments Nu Sapphire | IsotopX Phoenix | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Type of ICP-MS system. Multi-collector sector-field instruments combine a magnetic sector and electrostatic analyser with a fixed array of Faraday cups (and optionally ion counters) that simultaneously collect multiple isotope beams, enabling high-precision static multi-collection.
Example / Allowed Content: Multi-collector sector-field (MC-ICP-MS) | Other: specify

Metadata Item: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
Description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit. Supports traceability to instrument service records.
Type of plasma torch used (e.g., standard quartz, high-matrix, low-flow).
Example / Allowed Content: Standard quartz | High-matrix | Low-flow | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Geometry and designation of the sampler and skimmer cones installed during analysis. For Neptune-type instruments, H-cones (standard) and X-cones (high-sensitivity, ~3× higher transmission) are common options; the choice affects ion beam intensity and is a procedure design decision. Jet cones combined with an interface pump upgrade are used on some instruments for enhanced sensitivity.
Example / Allowed Content: Ni H-sampler + Ni H-skimmer (standard) | Ni H-sampler + Ni X-skimmer | Ni Jet-sampler + Ni X-skimmer (with interface pump) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Material composition of the sampler and skimmer cones. Nickel (Ni) is standard for HNO3 matrices. Platinum (Pt) cones are used for HCl-rich matrices (e.g., 6 M HCl in Fe chemistry procedures) due to greater corrosion resistance.
Example / Allowed Content: Ni sampler and Ni skimmer | Pt sampler and Pt skimmer | Ni sampler and Pt skimmer | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm). Affects ion transmission efficiency and oxide formation rates. Procedure registers the target torch position; analyst confirms or adjusts during session tuning.
Example / Allowed Content: 5 mm | Standard position (manufacturer default) | N/A | None

Description: Whether a guard electrode (grounded shield electrode) is installed and active on the torch assembly. Capacitively decouples the plasma from the load coil, reducing secondary discharge and improving ion extraction efficiency.
Example / Allowed Content: On | Off | Not installed | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Description of the multi-collector Faraday cup array. Specify the total number of Faraday cup detectors (fixed and moveable), their labeled positions (e.g., L4, L3, L2, L1, Ax, H1, H2, H3, H4 for a 9-cup Neptune), and the presence and position of any ion counter (SEM) or Daly detector in the collector block. The number and span of cups constrains which isotope combinations can be simultaneously collected.
Example / Allowed Content: Neptune: 9 Faraday cups (L4–H4) + 1 SEM (axial or off-axis); Nu Plasma II: 16 Faraday cups + 3 ion counters | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Resistance values (Ω) of the feedback resistors in the Faraday cup amplifiers. Standard amplifiers use 10¹¹ Ω resistors, yielding 1 V per ~6.24 × 10⁶ ion counts per second. High-gain amplifiers (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) are fitted to selected cups to improve signal-to-noise for very low-intensity beams (e.g., 234U, low-abundance spike isotopes). Report the resistor value per cup position, or note 'all 10¹¹ Ω' if uniform.
Example / Allowed Content: All cups: 10¹¹ Ω | L1: 10¹³ Ω (234U); all others: 10¹¹ Ω | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Method used to calibrate the relative gain (amplification factor) of each Faraday cup amplifier at the start of or during each analytical session. Relative gain differences between amplifiers cause systematic errors in isotope ratios if uncorrected. Common approaches: instrument internal gain calibration routine (measures signal in each cup sequentially using a common beam), amplifier rotation procedure, or measurement of a known isotope ratio solution in each cup. For instruments with SEM detectors, also describes the SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration sequence. Specify frequency (per session, per block, weekly).
Example / Allowed Content: Instrument internal gain calibration routine; baseline and gain calibrated at session start and daily | SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration measured per session using known ratio solution | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Mass resolution mode used in this procedure. MC-ICP-MS instruments allow selection of low resolution (LR; m/Δm ≈ 300–400), medium resolution (MR; m/Δm ≈ 3000–8000), or high resolution (HR; m/Δm ≈ 10,000–12,000). Most isotope ratio measurements use low resolution after chemical separation has removed interfering elements. Medium or high resolution is used when polyatomic interferences (e.g., ArN+, ArO+, ArOH+ on Fe isotopes) cannot be fully resolved by chemistry alone. Procedure registers the mode in use; analyst confirms at session start.
Example / Allowed Content: LR (m/Δm ≈ 300) | MR (m/Δm ≈ 3000–8000) | HR (m/Δm ≈ 10000–12000) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Whether a collision or reaction cell is installed and its operating mode for this procedure. Most conventional multi-collector instruments have no cell — mass bias and isobaric interferences are handled entirely by chemical separation and mass-bias correction (record 'Not installed'). A small number of modern MC-ICP-MS instruments (e.g., Nu Instruments Sapphire, Thermo Scientific Neoma MS/MS) add a hexapole collision/reaction cell upstream of the collector array, operated in STD/KED/DRC modes analogous to quadrupole ICP-MS/MS instruments, to suppress polyatomic and isobaric interferences before simultaneous multi-collection. Specific gas types, flow rates, and voltages are documented in Group 4.
Example / Allowed Content: Not installed | STD (standard mode, no gas) | KED (kinetic energy discrimination, He gas) | DRC (dynamic reaction cell, reactive gas) | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Type and material of the pneumatic nebulizer used for sample introduction. Affects droplet size distribution and uptake rate.
Example / Allowed Content: PFA self-aspirating MicroFlow (50–100 µL/min) | PFA-ST | Glass concentric | ESI Apex-HF nebulizer | N/A | None | Other: specify

Metadata Item: Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperature
Description: Type of spray chamber and cooling temperature if thermostatted (°C). Chamber type and temperature control aerosol droplet size and solvent vapor load reaching the plasma. Scott double-pass and cyclonic chambers are standard; in some procedures a spray chamber is placed downstream of a desolvating nebulizer to improve signal stability.
Example / Allowed Content: Stable Introduction System (SIS): cyclonic + Scott double-pass | Scott double-pass (glass) at 2°C | Cyclonic at 5°C | Spray chamber downstream of Aridus II | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Desolvating nebulizer or membrane desolvator used upstream of the plasma to reduce solvent load, increase sensitivity, and lower oxide production rates. Frequently used in MC-ICP-MS for low-abundance isotopes or small sample sizes. Note that desolvation can introduce additional instrumental mass bias instability compared to wet introduction systems. Record 'None' if not used.
Example / Allowed Content: Aridus II | Aridus I | Apex-IR | Apex-HF | ApexQ | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Peristaltic pump speed or self-aspiration flow rate for sample introduction (µL/min or mL/min).
Name and version of the software used to control the instrument and acquire raw multi-collector data.

Name and version of the software used for data reduction: baseline subtraction, gain correction, mass bias correction (SSB, double-spike inversion, or internal normalization), interference corrections, and calculation of isotope ratios, δ-values, and concentrations. Include version number.
Radiofrequency forward power applied to the plasma (W). Controls ionization efficiency and oxide production rates.
Flow rate of the outer (coolant) argon gas stream (L/min). Influences plasma temperature and oxide ion formation.
Example / Allowed Content: 13–16 L/min

Description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream between torch body and injector tube (L/min).
Flow rate of the carrier argon gas delivered through the nebulizer (L/min). Controls aerosol transport and strongly influences signal sensitivity and stability. Adjusted daily to optimize signal.
Supplementary argon flow added downstream of a desolvation system to maintain total gas delivery to the plasma (L/min). Record 'N/A' if no desolvation system is used.
Comments: Only relevant when Desolvation System is not 'None'

Description: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under normal (hot) or cool plasma conditions. Normal plasma (>1000 W RF) is standard for solution MC-ICP-MS. Cool plasma is rarely used in MC-ICP-MS due to stability requirements for high-precision isotope ratio work.
Example / Allowed Content: Normal plasma | Cool plasma | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Element(s) whose isotopic composition or concentration is determined by this procedure. In solution MC-ICP-MS the analyte is typically a single element isotope system (e.g., Fe, U, Sn, Pb, Zn) or multiple elements when the measurement simultaneously yields isotope ratios and isotope dilution concentrations. The procedure registers the primary analyte element(s); at analysis level the analyst records the actual suite measured. The complete mass list and cup assignments are documented in Collector Configuration.

Assignment of isotope masses to Faraday cup or ion counter detector positions for this procedure. Lists the mass number monitored in each collector position (e.g., L4=116Sn, L3=117Sn, L2=118Sn, L1=119Sn, Ax=120Sn, H1=121Sb, H2=122Sn, H3=123Sb, H4=124Sn). For static multi-collection procedures, one configuration applies throughout the measurement. For multi-dynamic procedures, list all configurations and the cycling sequence. Includes all interference-monitor masses collected in addition to analyte isotopes. Analyte-specific: different element systems require different mass assignments within the collector array span.

Number of measurement blocks acquired per sample or standard solution introduction. In MC-ICP-MS, data are structured as blocks of cycles; each block typically begins with a baseline (on-peak zero) measurement before the analytical cycles. Multiple blocks per sample allow inspection of signal stability and within-measurement drift. Procedure specifies the standard number; analyst may adjust for samples with low signal or for high-precision requirements.

Number of measurement cycles acquired per block. One cycle corresponds to a single set of simultaneous Faraday cup readings integrated for the duration specified in Integration Time per Cycle. Total integration time per sample = (Number of Cycles per Block) × (Integration Time per Cycle) × (Number of Blocks per Measurement). Procedure specifies the standard value; analyst may adjust within procedure bounds.

Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle (seconds). Determines counting statistics per cycle. Longer integration times improve shot-noise precision but increase the impact of signal drift within the integration window. For high-gain (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) amplifier channels, longer integration times are often required to accumulate sufficient charge. Procedure specifies the standard integration time; analyst may confirm or adjust within procedure bounds. Analyte-specific when different isotope channels use different integration schemes.

Method and timing for measuring the ion beam baseline (on-peak zero) during acquisition. In MC-ICP-MS, the baseline is measured at the start of each block by deflecting the ion beam (beam-off or electrostatic deflector) or by aspiring an acid blank solution, and integrating for a set number of cycles. The baseline signal is subtracted from all subsequent analytical cycles in that block. Specify: (1) baseline method (beam deflector / acid blank solution), (2) number of baseline cycles per block, (3) solution used for on-peak zero (same acid matrix as samples, e.g., 0.3 M HNO3). This field documents the acquisition procedure; the choice of blank correction approach is in Blank/Background Correction Method (Group 5).
Example / Allowed Content: Beam deflector on-peak zero; 1 baseline block of 1 cycle (4.194 s) per measurement block | On-peak zero measured before each sample by aspirating 0.3 M HNO3 for 10 cycles | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Duration of instrument rinse between successive sample solutions (seconds). Controls carryover and memory effects. For isotope ratio work, complete washout is critical to prevent cross-contamination between samples with differing isotopic compositions.

Description of the measurement order within a session: how sample solutions, bracketing standards, secondary reference materials, and blanks are interleaved. For SSB procedures, each sample is bracketed by two standards (standard–sample–standard); the bracketing standard is the same isotopic material as the zero-delta reference. For double-spike procedures, standards are spiked to the same level as samples before analysis.
Example / Allowed Content: SSB: sample bracketed by two standards (Std1–Sample–Std2) | Double-spike: spiked standards bracketing spiked samples | SSB + secondary RM every 5 samples | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Type of collision gas used in KED mode for polyatomic interference suppression, on collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS). Record 'N/A' if the instrument has no cell or KED mode is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: He | H2 | He+H2 | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: KED; only applicable to collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments

Description: Flow rate of the collision gas in KED mode (mL/min), on collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments. Higher flow rates provide greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity. Record 'N/A' if the instrument has no cell or KED mode is not used.
Comments: KED; only applicable to collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments

Description: Kinetic energy discrimination offset voltage applied at the exit of the collision cell (V), on collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments. Controls the degree of polyatomic ion suppression. Record 'N/A' if the instrument has no cell or KED mode is not used.
Comments: KED; only applicable to collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments

Description: Type of reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (e.g., NH3, O2, CH4), on collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments. Record 'N/A' if the instrument has no cell or DRC mode is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: NH3 | O2 | CH4 | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: DRC; only applicable to collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments

Description: Flow rate of the reaction gas in DRC mode (mL/min), on collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments. Record 'N/A' if the instrument has no cell or DRC mode is not used.
Comments: DRC; only applicable to collision/reaction-cell-equipped MC-ICP-MS instruments

Description: Element added at a known concentration to all sample and standard solutions to serve as an internal normalization standard for mass bias correction (SSB + internal normalization procedures). The element must have a known isotopic composition and mass similar to the analyte. Examples: Ni or Cu doping for Fe isotopes (must verify complete matrix separation); Tl for Pb isotopes; Cd for Sb isotopes. Specify element and monitored isotope. Record 'None' if SSB without internal standard or double-spike method is used.
Example / Allowed Content: Cu (65Cu/63Cu for Fe procedures) | Ni (62Ni/58Ni for Fe procedures) | Tl (205Tl/203Tl for Pb procedures) | Cd (113Cd/111Cd for Sb procedures) | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Target concentration of the internal normalization standard element in all measured solutions (µg/L).
Comments: Only relevant when Internal Standard Element is not 'None'

Description: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. CeO+/Ce+ (m/z 156/140) is the standard monitor proxy. Record both the monitored mass ratio(s) and the maximum allowed threshold(s). Stricter oxide thresholds may be required for analytes sensitive to oxide interferences (e.g., BaO+ on REE isotopes). Measured values are recorded in Oxide Production.
Example / Allowed Content: CeO+/Ce+ (m/z 156/140) < 0.5% | CeO+/Ce+ < 0.3%; BaO+/Ba+ (m/z 154/138) < 0.1% | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Measured oxide production ratio obtained during session-start tuning, for the proxy specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold. Record the measured value and confirm whether the procedure threshold was met.
Example / Allowed Content: CeO+/Ce+ = 0.3% (threshold < 0.5% met) | BaO+/Ba+ = 0.07% (threshold < 0.1% met)

Description: Primary strategy used to correct for instrumental isotopic mass fractionation. In solution MC-ICP-MS, instrumental mass bias is typically 3–5%/amu and must be corrected before isotope ratios can be interpreted geochemically. Four main strategies: (1) Sample-standard bracketing (SSB): alternating sample and isotopic standard measurements; bias interpolated linearly between bracketing measurements. (2) Double-spike: a mixture of two enriched isotopes of the analyte element added before digestion provides an internal monitor of both instrumental and chemical mass fractionation. (3) Internal normalization: an element of known isotopic composition added to samples and standards; measured ratio of normalizing element used to calculate the mass bias factor applied to analyte ratios. (4) SSB + internal normalization: both strategies applied simultaneously for redundant bias correction.
Example / Allowed Content: SSB | Double-spike | Internal normalization | SSB + internal normalization | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Mathematical law used to parameterize instrumental isotope mass fractionation as a function of mass difference. The exponential law (Maréchal et al. 1999) is most widely used and theoretically best justified for MC-ICP-MS. The linear law assumes fractionation proportional to mass difference. The power law is an alternative formulation. For double-spike procedures, the law is embedded in the inversion algorithm and must be consistent between spike calibration and sample data reduction.
Example / Allowed Content: Exponential | Linear | Power | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: The pair of enriched isotopes used to construct the double spike. Both isotopes must be naturally rare, free from isobaric interferences, and chosen to minimize error magnification in the inversion. The double spike composition must be accurately calibrated before use. Specify both isotope masses and the spike certificate or calibration reference. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: 233U–236U (IRMM-3636) | 117Sn–122Sn (in-house calibrated) | 57Fe–58Fe | 61Ni–62Ni | 204Pb–207Pb | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Double-spike only; record 'N/A' if not applicable

Description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total analyte signal in the spiked mixture, expressed as spike fraction (0–1) or spike:sample ratio. An optimal mixing ratio minimizes error propagation through the double-spike inversion; the optimum is analyte-system specific and is typically determined using the Double Spike Toolbox or equivalent. The achieved mixing ratio may deviate from the target within acceptable bounds (typically ±20% of optimal); the double-spike inversion corrects for actual mixing ratios. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: ~0.40 (spike fraction; optimal for 117Sn–122Sn) | ~0.5 spike:sample | N/A | None
Comments: Double-spike only; record 'N/A' if not applicable. C=Advanced vs Basic: pending lit assessment

Description: Mathematical algorithm used to simultaneously solve for the true sample isotope ratio and the mass fractionation factor from the measured spike-sample mixture. Common implementations: iterative Newton-Raphson solution, matrix algebraic approach, or published software (e.g., Rudge et al. 2009 Double Spike Toolbox). Specify the algorithm or software reference and version. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: Rudge et al. (2009) Double Spike Toolbox | Iterative Newton-Raphson (Compston & Oversby 1969) | In-house spreadsheet implementing exponential-law inversion | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Double-spike only; record 'N/A' if not applicable

Metadata Item: Internal Normalization Element and Isotope Ratio
Description: Element and isotope ratio used as the internal normalization standard for mass bias correction. The measured ratio of the normalizing element is used to calculate the mass bias factor β using the chosen mass fractionation law, which is then applied to correct the analyte isotope ratios assuming β_norm ≈ β_analyte. Specify the element, the monitored isotope ratio (e.g., 113Cd/111Cd for Sb measurements), and the certified or consensus value used for correction. Record 'N/A' if internal normalization is not used.
Example / Allowed Content: 60Ni/58Ni = 0.38579 (from IUPAC 2021) for Fe-Ni doping | 65Cu/63Cu = 0.44561 for Fe-Cu doping | 113Cd/111Cd = 0.95542 (Abouchami et al. 2012) for Sb | 205Tl/203Tl = 2.38714 for Pb | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Internal normalization only; record 'N/A' if not applicable

Description: Specific isotope ratio pair(s) reported as primary data output. The denominator isotope is typically the reference mass used in the delta notation (e.g., 54Fe for Fe isotopes, 235U for U isotopes). Report all ratio pairs routinely calculated and reported. Analyte-specific.
Example / Allowed Content: 56Fe/54Fe and 57Fe/54Fe | 238U/235U | 122Sn/118Sn | 123Sb/121Sb | 206Pb/204Pb; 207Pb/204Pb; 208Pb/204Pb | N/A | None | Other: specify

Metadata Item: delta or epsilon Value Reference Standard
Description: International or community-accepted isotopic reference standard used as the zero-delta anchor for expressing isotopic compositions in delta (δ, per mil) or epsilon (ε, per ten thousand) notation: δⁱX = [(ⁱX/ʲX)sample / (ⁱX/ʲX)reference − 1] × 1000‰. The reporting reference is a per-study or per-publication decision and is specified at analysis level. Specify the standard name, lot or batch number where applicable, and the certified or consensus isotope ratio used for normalization. Analyte-specific.
Example / Allowed Content: IRMM-014 (Fe; Taylor et al. 1992) | CRM-112a / SRM-960 (U) | NIST SRM 981 (Pb) | NIST SRM 3102a (Sb) | Sn_IPGP (in-house Sn standard) | JMC Lyon (Zn) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Approach used to convert measured ion signals to elemental concentrations, where concentration data are also a product of the procedure (e.g., isotope dilution combined with isotope ratio measurement). For procedures producing isotope ratios only (no concentration output), record 'Not applicable (isotope ratios only)'. For double-spike procedures that simultaneously yield concentrations, record the ID calculation approach. Analyte-specific when different elements use different strategies.
Example / Allowed Content: Not applicable (isotope ratios only) | Isotope dilution via double-spike inversion (concentrations co-determined with isotope ratios) | IUPAC isotope dilution equations (separate ID spike) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Method used to define which portion of the acquisition signal is integrated for each measurement. In MC-ICP-MS, all cycles within a block are typically used unless signal instability is detected. Specify the rule for including or excluding individual cycles.
Example / Allowed Content: All cycles included unless signal instability detected | Visual inspection of cycle-by-cycle data; outlier cycles excluded manually | Automated 2σ outlier rejection per block | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Total integration time per sample solution (s). Calculated from blocks × cycles per block × integration time per cycle. Recorded at analysis level as the actual total time used.

Method used to subtract instrument background from analytical signals. In MC-ICP-MS, on-peak zero subtraction (aspirating the same acid matrix as samples while measuring background at the analyte masses with beam deflector or from baseline cycles at the start of each block) is standard. For isotope ratio procedures where procedural blank is minor relative to the sample signal, on-peak zero is often sufficient. For low-level analyses, procedural blank must be measured and subtracted.
Example / Allowed Content: On-peak zero (acid blank) | Procedural blank | On-peak zero + procedural blank | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous cycles or replicate measurements from the calculated isotope ratio mean. Filtering is applied after baseline subtraction and before mass bias correction.
Example / Allowed Content: 2σ exclusion on per-cycle ratios | Grubbs test | Visual inspection | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Whether mathematical corrections for residual isobaric or polyatomic interferences are applied in data reduction, supplementary to any interference suppression achieved by chemical separation or mass resolution. In solution MC-ICP-MS, chemical separation is the primary interference mitigation; mathematical corrections address residual contributions. Common examples: 204Hg on 204Pb; abundance sensitivity tailing of 238U onto 236U and 235U. Analyte-specific.
Example / Allowed Content: Y | N | Analyte-specific | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: List of isobaric or polyatomic species mathematically corrected in data reduction. Includes direct isobars (e.g., 54Cr+ on 54Fe+, 58Ni+ on 58Fe+), abundance sensitivity tailing (e.g., 238U tail on 235U and 236U in U isotope measurements), and hydride interferences (e.g., 238UH+ at mass 239). Analyte-specific.
Example / Allowed Content: 54Cr+ on 54Fe+; 58Ni+ on 58Fe+ | 204Hg+ on 204Pb (corrected via 202Hg monitor) | 238U abundance sensitivity tail on 235U and 236U | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Mathematical approach used to calculate and remove residual interference contributions. For direct isobars, interference monitor masses (e.g., 202Hg to correct 204Hg on 204Pb) are measured simultaneously and used with natural abundance ratios to calculate the interference contribution. For abundance sensitivity, the tailing factor is measured using a pure standard. Analyte-specific.
Example / Allowed Content: Monitor mass correction: 202Hg signal × (204Hg/202Hg)natural to correct 204Pb | Abundance sensitivity tailing factor measured weekly from pure U standard | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample isotope ratios and/or elemental concentrations from spike-sample mixture measurements. For double-spike procedures, isotope ratios and concentrations are co-determined through the spike inversion. For conventional ID concentration procedures (separate concentration spike), IUPAC ID equations are used. Record 'None' if neither isotope dilution nor double-spike methods are used.
Example / Allowed Content: Double-spike inversion (isotope ratios and concentrations co-determined) | IUPAC isotope dilution equations (concentration from separate ID spike) | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Procedure applied to minimize carryover of analyte isotopes between successive sample introductions. In MC-ICP-MS, extended rinse periods with the same acid matrix as samples (see Wash Time Between Samples) are the primary mitigation. At data processing level, documents any flagging or exclusion of measurements preceded by samples with significantly different isotopic compositions where carryover may be suspected.
Example / Allowed Content: Extended acid rinse between samples; first measurement excluded if preceded by high-signal sample | Blank measurement inspected before each sample; session halted if blank > 0.5% of sample signal | None required for this analyte suite | N/A | None

Description: Method used to propagate analytical uncertainties from raw isotope ratios through to final δ or ε values. For SSB procedures, uncertainty is typically calculated from the reproducibility of bracketing standard measurements. For double-spike procedures, uncertainty is propagated through the inversion using error propagation equations or Monte Carlo simulation.
Example / Allowed Content: 2σ of bracketing standard reproducibility propagated to sample | Monte Carlo simulation through double-spike inversion | ISO GUM quadrature propagation | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to output isotope ratio data beyond the primary mass bias correction. Examples: correction of δ values for decay of enriched spike isotopes between calibration and use date (double-spike procedures); age correction of δ238U for secular disequilibrium. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: Spike isotope decay correction applied | Age correction for U-series disequilibrium | None | N/A | Other: specify

Description: Physical constants and reference values used in data reduction to calculate the final reported quantity (e.g., decay constants for age calculation, standard isotope ratios, or other citable reference values used in a correction or calculation), together with their source. Distinct from Reference Material Information / Secondary Reference Materials (Group 6), which document accepted values for specific calibration/validation materials rather than universal physical constants. Record "None" if no citable, revisable physical constants feed into this procedure's data reduction.

Name and reference material identifier of the isotopic reference standard used as the bracketing standard (SSB) or zero-delta anchor. This is an isotopic composition standard (not a concentration standard): it defines the isotopic composition against which all sample δ or ε values are normalized. Must be a pure, homogeneous, internationally distributed material with well-characterized isotopic composition. For double-spike procedures, also used for spike calibration.
Example / Allowed Content: IRMM-014 (Fe isotopes; Taylor et al. 1992) | CRM-112a / SRM-960 (U isotopes) | NIST SRM 981 (Pb isotopes) | JMC Lyon Zn standard | NIST SRM 3102a (Sb) | In-house single-element standard solution: specify | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: How often the primary isotopic standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session. For SSB, typically one standard measurement before and one after each sample (standard–sample–standard triplet). Specify the bracketing scheme.
Example / Allowed Content: SSB: one standard before and one after every sample | One standard every 3 samples | Start and end of session only | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Reference material(s) measured as unknowns to independently assess analytical accuracy. Specify material name and the isotopic composition reference source (certified value, consensus value, or literature compilation). For isotope ratio procedures, secondary RMs are geological materials with published isotopic compositions (e.g., BHVO-2 for Fe isotopes) or pure isotopic standards of certified composition.
Example / Allowed Content: BHVO-2 (Fe isotopes; Dauphas & Rouxel 2006 compilation) | BCR-2 | NIST SRM 960 or equivalent U standard | NIST SRM 981 (Pb) | AGV-2 | N/A | None | Other: specify

Metadata Item: In-Run Isotope Ratio Reproducibility and Assessment Method
Description: Reproducibility of isotope ratio or δ-value measurements within a single analytical session and the method used to assess it. For solution MC-ICP-MS, precision is reported as 2σ (two standard deviations) or 2SE (two standard errors of the mean) on replicate analyses of an isotopic standard or secondary reference material run as an unknown during the session. Specify: (1) the metric (2σ, 2SD, 2SE, 95% CI); (2) the reference material or standard analyzed; (3) the number of replicate measurements; (4) the ratio pair or δ value assessed. Example: 2SD = 0.03‰ on δ56Fe (n = 10 BHVO-2 analyses in session).
Example / Allowed Content: 2SD = 0.03‰ on δ56Fe (n=10 BHVO-2); session | 2σ = 0.004‰ on δ238U (n=9 CRM-112a brackets) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Reproducibility of isotope ratio or δ-value measurements across multiple analytical sessions (long-term external reproducibility) and the method used to assess it. Typically expressed as 2SD of repeated independent measurements of a secondary reference material across sessions over weeks to months. Specify: (1) the metric; (2) the reference material; (3) the number of measurements and sessions; (4) the ratio or δ value assessed.
Example / Allowed Content: 2SD = 0.030‰ on δ56Fe (n=23 sessions; BHVO-1; Dauphas et al. 2009) | 2SD = 0.005‰ on δ238U (n > 50 analyses; CRM-112a) | N/A | None | Other: specify

Description: Accuracy of isotope ratio or δ-value measurements relative to certified or published consensus values and the method used to assess it. For isotope ratio procedures, accuracy is typically assessed by comparing measured δ values for secondary geological reference materials against published interlaboratory compilations or certified values.
Example / Allowed Content: % deviation from published δ56Fe for BHVO-1 compilation value | Agreement with certified δ238U of IRMM-3636 spike solution | Z-score relative to interlaboratory consensus | N/A | None | Other: specify
